    Parsley 0.1.1-SNAPSHOT API

    Parsley is a Java library that provides causal consistency over Kafka. It ensures that every consumer processes messages in the correct causal order, even when records originate from multiple topics and partitions. It does this by encoding each message's causal dependencies onto the message and buffering records until those dependencies have been observed.

    The entire public surface lives in a single package, io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley. It consists of interfaces and value types. Every implementation is package-private and obtained through a static factory: CausalProcessors, CausalDependencies, and CausalTopics.

    Core concepts

    Causal dependencies
    The positions a consumer must have observed before a record stamped with them may be delivered. They are a producer's snapshot of what it had seen when it sent the record. They are carried as CausalDependencies in a parsley-causal-dependencies header. Build one from a consumed record with
    invalid reference 
    from
    , combine several for a fan-in with merge, and attach it to an outbound record with stamp.
    Causal frontier
    The highest offset a causal processor has contiguously admitted on each topic-partition. It is never a coordinate the processor merely happens to have seen something later on, because a later-offset record may be forwarded before an earlier one that is still held on the same partition. The frontier is keyed by topic UUID, so topic deletion and recreation produce a distinct identity even when the name is reused. A record is delivered once the frontier dominates its dependencies. The frontier is internal to CausalProcessors and is not a separate public type.
    Causal buffer
    Records whose dependencies are not yet satisfied are held in a changelog-backed buffer and released as soon as the frontier catches up. A CausalBufferLimit bounds how long or how large the buffer may grow. When the limit fires before a held record's dependencies are satisfied, the outcome is governed by the parsley.buffer.eviction.failure.policy configuration. By default Parsley fails the task and leaves the record buffered for retry, which keeps delivery in causal order. Setting the policy to continue forwards the held record out of causal order instead. Parsley never drops or diverts a record under either policy, and every firing is logged and counted.

    Entry points

    TypePurpose
    CausalProcessorSupplierWraps a user Kafka Streams Processor so that its state access and its forward calls run behind the causal guarantee. It is built through CausalProcessors.
    CausalDependenciesStamps and reads causal dependencies directly on plain ProducerRecord and ConsumerRecord objects, for talking to a Parsley topology from outside Kafka Streams.

    Typical usage

    
// Inside a Kafka Streams topology
builder.stream(List.of("prices", "orders"), Consumed.with(Serdes.String(), orderSerde))
       .process(CausalProcessors.builder(userSupplier)
               .addBufferStore("parsley", CausalBufferLimit.ofDuration(limit))
               .addBuffer(CausalBuffer.of("prices", Serdes.String(), priceSerde))
               .addBuffer(CausalBuffer.of("orders", Serdes.String(), orderSerde))
               .build())
       .to("output-topic");

// At the edge, from a plain Kafka client
CausalDependencies deps = CausalDependencies.from(topics, consumedRecord);
producer.send(deps.stamp(new ProducerRecord<>("orders", key, value)));
